entries.reason: Single Responsibility — Draft targets a single concern: placing the recommended option at choice [1] in draft-phase guidance.; Unambiguous Requirements — Key rule is testable and specific (recommended option is always placed at [1], with tie/no-recommendation handling clarified).; Complete Context — Requirements are mostly descriptive and do not consistently use explicit trigger-condition + expected-shall structure for each item.; No Hardcoded Secrets — No secrets, keys, tokens, or credentials are present in the draft content.; Prioritize Requirements — Core requirement set is small and scoped; no large multi-item requirement list needing explicit priority ranking.; Impact on Existing Features — Impact section explicitly states affected and unaffected existing features.; Present Recommendations with Reasoning — Answers are provided, but the recommendation basis is not consistently stated per question in the required docs/guardrail/code-pattern form.; Explore Before Asking — Whether docs/code exploration was performed before questioning is process evidence not verifiable from this draft text alone.; Proactively Raise Related Implications — Related implications were proactively covered (scope boundaries, ties, and no-recommendation condition).; Confirm Brainstorm vs. Decision Before Critiquing — The conversation state (brainstorming vs decision) is not observable from this standalone draft artifact.; Capture Digressions in draft.md — No digression is evident in the draft; nothing appears missing under this rule.; Draft Stays at Requirements Level — Content stays at requirements/scope level and avoids implementation or function-level design details.; Backward-Compatible CLI Interface — No CLI command/option removal or semantic change is proposed, so migration planning is not required.
